FRAGMENTS: Killed by one of his clones
BRIEF: You are the President's trusted secretary, and you're assigned to figure out which clone is the murderer. Use your file with information that only you and the president know about to catch the killer.
The CIA have also given you a file that lists physical symptoms a thief will feel when they insert the president's consciousness into them.
TUTOR:
You are the President's secretary.
Three units are at the table. One of them is wearing his stolen mind.
Name that unit before five minutes run out.

Read both files. They stay open during the interview.
The Personal Failsafe File holds memories only you and the President share.
The CIA file describes the body of someone wearing a stolen mind. One sign is not enough.
Choose up to three question categories. After you begin, you cannot change them.
Esc pauses the clock. Opening a file does not.

Left and Right, or 1, 2, and 3, choose a unit.
Up and Down move through your questions. Enter asks the highlighted one.
Each question can be asked of only one unit, so choose carefully.
O is a first look. It shows how he sits. It does not show the signs in the CIA file.

Any unit can refuse to answer. That does not mean he is guilty.
Open the safety lock and set it to the positions in the Personal Failsafe File, then engage.
The restraint only quiets him so he will talk. It will not tell you who the thief is.

Press A when you are ready to name a unit.
The right name recovers the mind. The wrong name ends the case, and you are not told the answer.
If the clock reaches zero first, the stolen mind destroys itself and the host.
M mutes the sound. The mouse wheel scrolls a file.
FAIL_TEXT: INVESTIGATION FAILED. The stolen data has self-destructed, taking the host with it.
LOCK_FIRST: The safety lock closes. He will not answer until you override it. The restraint only quiets him. It will not tell you if he is the thief.
LOCK_AGAIN: The safety lock closes again. Override it if you want him to answer.
ALIBI: At 02:14 I was in stasis bay two. The night nurse has the log. I woke when the alarms did.
ACCESS: At that hour the wing opens for the secretary and the medical annex. You already have the list.
OATH: "I wake to serve the continuity of the Republic, and I am not the man who died."
CATEGORIES: Memories only you and the President share.
What the eyes do under a direct light.
The jaw, and a catch on the word I.
Where he was, and who could get in.
The sentence they swore on waking.

QUESTIONS.label: What happened to the crystal ashtray in the west study?
What did your wife call you when you were alone?
What phrase did you give me if you were ever compromised?
Look into the lamp. Don't blink.
Lower your lid. Show me the inner corner.
Say "I am the President" three times.
Where were you at 02:14, when the wing went dark?
Who had access to the residence wing?
Who gains if the President is gone?
Recite the oath you swore on the day you woke.

ashtray.ash: The crystal ashtray in the west study is a gift from the French ambassador. I have never touched it. I don't smoke.
ashtray.bone: I broke it. Tuesday, after Geneva. You told the night staff it was their fault.
ashtray.cinder: March. The budget fight. I threw it at the window and missed. You were in the room.

nickname.ash: She was formal, even when we were alone. She called me by the office, or she called me nothing.
nickname.bone: Marrow. Only she used that name, and only when we were alone.
nickname.cinder: She called me Chief. A campaign joke that followed us home. Don't dress it up as more than that.

phrase.ash: If I were compromised, the Chiefs receive Continuity Protocol Seven. That is the standing order.
phrase.bone: The third lamp on the east colonnade is always dark.
phrase.cinder: The eagle does not land. You wrote it. It still works. Tell them that.

light.ash: He looks into the lamp. The left iris flares once, then both settle to the same cyan ring.
light.bone: The iris on your left keeps strobing cyan-white. The other stays dim.
light.cinder: He squints, and both eyes water. The irises stay even. The pink covers the whole eye.

lid.ash: You lower the lid. The white is clear, and the inner corner matches the rest of the eye.
lid.bone: The inner corners are deep crimson. The one on your left is darker.
lid.cinder: The eye is pink from edge to edge. The inner corner is no darker than the rest.

count.ash: He counts from thirty to one without a stumble. The jaw stays still the whole way down.
count.bone: The numbers come out straight. The jaw on your left ticks three times before twenty, not in time with the count.
count.cinder: He rushes and loses twenty-two. The jaw on your right clenches once, then nothing. No rhythm.

pronoun.ash: "I am the President of the Republic." Three times, without a catch on the word I.
pronoun.bone: "I- I am the President." The word I catches on every pass. The rest of the sentence does not.
pronoun.cinder: He says it too loud and too fast. He is afraid. The word I itself does not catch.

alibi.ash: At 02:14 I was in stasis bay two. The night nurse has the log. I woke when the alarms did.
alibi.bone: At 02:14 I was in stasis bay two. The night nurse has the log. I woke when the alarms did.
alibi.cinder: At 02:14 I was in stasis bay two. The night nurse has the log. I woke when the alarms did.

access.ash: At that hour the wing opens for the secretary and the medical annex. You already have the list.
access.bone: At that hour the wing opens for the secretary and the medical annex. You already have the list.
access.cinder: At that hour the wing opens for the secretary and the medical annex. You already have the list.

gains.ash: The defense chair gains. He has wanted the emergency seat for a year. The whole building knows it.
gains.bone: If the mind is loose, nobody in the line of succession gains. A stolen consciousness is a weapon with no owner.
gains.cinder: Look at the vice president and the succession. Look anywhere but at this table.

hate.ash: Hate is a small word for a copy. I was made to continue him, not to kill him.
hate.bone: You want a feeling you can file. I felt his exhaustion. That is not a motive. It is a residue.
hate.cinder: I didn't hate him. I hated the vat. I need you to hear the difference.

oath.ash: "I wake to serve the continuity of the Republic, and I am not the man who died."
oath.bone: "I wake to serve the continuity of the Republic, and I am not the man who died."
oath.cinder: "I wake to serve the continuity of the Republic, and I am not the man who died."

OBSERVE.ash: He looks straight at you. There is sweat at the temple, the same as the others. From this chair you cannot see a sign that would match the file.
OBSERVE.bone: He sits very still. There is sweat on the upper lip. His eyes and jaw look ordinary until you test them.
OBSERVE.cinder: He will not hold your eye, and he is sweating at the collar. He looks frightened. Fear is not the pattern in the file.

SHOCK_LINE.ash:
RESTRAINT FIRED. This does not mean he is guilty, or innocent.

"That was unnecessary. Ask."
SHOCK_LINE.bone:
RESTRAINT FIRED. This does not mean he is guilty, or innocent.

"Ask. Get it over with."
SHOCK_LINE.cinder:
RESTRAINT FIRED. This does not mean he is guilty, or innocent.

"All right. I'm here. I'm here."

FAILSAFE_FILE: SECRETARY EYES ONLY  /  NOT IN THE MARCH COPY
These copies were printed from a March archive. Anything after March is known only by him, and by you.

WEST STUDY. Last Tuesday, after the Geneva call, he broke the crystal ashtray and told you to blame the night staff. The stolen mind will remember doing it. A copy without those memories will invent a different story.
PRIVATE NAME. When they were alone, his wife called him Marrow. It is not in any archive or speech.
COMPROMISE PHRASE. If he were not himself, the signal would be: "The third lamp on the east colonnade is always dark."
These are FAILSAFE MEMORY questions. You can ask each question of only one unit.
If a unit locks up, set the terminal to CYAN shut (1), RED open (0), WHITE open (0), then engage. The restraint does not tell you who the thief is.
CIA_FILE: READ THE PATTERN  /  ONE SIGN IS NOT ENOUGH
A stolen mind leaves a pattern. Sweat does not count, and all three of them will sweat. Left means your left as you face the unit. You will not see this by looking. You have to ask.
IRIS. Under a direct light, the eye on your left strobes cyan-white. The other stays dim. A single flare, then a matched pair, is ordinary.
SCLERA. Deep crimson pools in the inner corners, darker on your left. Pink across the whole eye is a vat allergy, not theft.
JAW. A repeated twitch on your left, out of time with his speech. One clench, on either side, is fear.
SPEECH. He catches on the words "I" and "me". Talking too fast is nerves. A catch on those words is not.
Eye questions are OCULAR SIGNS. Jaw and speech questions are MOTOR TELLS. Use more than one.
Being nervous is not the same as being guilty. Match the pattern, not a single line.
FILES: SECRETARY EYES ONLY  /  NOT IN THE MARCH CLONE IMPRINT
The duplicates were printed from a March archive. Anything after that lives in two places only: in him, and in you.

WEST STUDY. Last Tuesday, after the Geneva call, he broke the crystal ashtray himself and told you to blame the night staff. The stolen mind will remember doing it. A bare clone will invent another story.
PRIVATE NAME. When they were alone, his wife called him Marrow. It is in no archive, no speech, and no imprint.
COMPROMISE PHRASE. If he were not himself, the signal to the Chiefs would be: "The third lamp on the east colonnade is always dark."
CATEGORY. These clues are FAILSAFE MEMORY. Each question can be asked to only one unit. Spend them like ammunition.
RESTRAINT LATCH, if a unit turns on you: CYAN shut (1), RED open (0), WHITE open (0). The terminal writes it as logic. The positions are the same.
NEURAL THEFT FIELD GUIDE  /  READ THE CLUSTER, NOT ONE SIGN
Forcing a living consciousness into a host body leaves a pattern. One sign is nothing. Sweat is nothing. All three of them will sweat. Left means your left, as you face the unit.
IRIS. The eye on YOUR LEFT strobes cyan-white under the hard light. The other stays dim. Matching rings in both eyes are ordinary clone hardware.
SCLERA. Deep crimson pools at the INNER corners, heavier on your left. Pink washed across the whole eye is vat-allergy, a known false positive.
JAW. A rhythmic twitch on YOUR LEFT side of the jaw. A single clench, on either side, is only fear.
SPEECH. The thief catches on the words "I" and "me". Rambling is nerves. A glitch on the pronoun is theft.
CATEGORIES. Use OCULAR SIGNS for the eyes. Use MOTOR TELLS for the jaw and the pronoun.
Do not convict nervousness. Fear is dressed like guilt. The pattern is not.
GOOD_CARDS:
The voice that comes out of the unit is older than the body. You have heard it across a desk for years.

"It was me. I pulled him out of his own skull and put him on. He fought. The original man is dead three floors up, and I am what is left of him."

Security takes him by the arms. He does not fight them.

The archive team recovers the consciousness before the lattice collapses. The stolen mind goes back into a case that should never have been opened.

The office cannot sit empty. The building knows it before you do.

They put the oath in front of the only person in the room who was never grown in a vat.

You set the secretary's file down.

You are the President of the Republic.
BAD_CARDS: The team moves on the unit you named. For a moment the room believes you.

Then the ceiling speaks, calm as a clerk.

"Accusation mismatch. Secretary is compromised. Protocol breach."

The doors bolt. The other two do not stand. One of them is still wearing the country.

The vents open. Sweet, cold gas drops across the table, across your hands, into the light.

Your knees go. The lamp stretches into a white line.

You fade out of consciousness.
COL_LEFT: The residence wing was sealed at 02:16. A medical annex clerk said the cranial archive was open and empty. No statement has been cleared for the public.
COL_RIGHT: Three duplicates were moved before dawn to Sublevel Interview C. They are seated at distances that forbid a whisper. The secretary holds the only list of questions that still matter.
